source_context_verses.text: The nations in Gilead gathered against the Israelites living in their territory to destroy them, and they fled into the stronghold of Dathema.
They sent letters to Judas and his brothers, saying, “The nations around us have gathered against us to destroy us.
They are preparing to come and seize the stronghold into which we fled, and Timothy is leading their force.
Now, therefore, come and rescue us from their hand, because many of us have fallen.
All our brothers in the region of Tobiah have been put to death. They have taken their wives, children, and belongings captive, and have destroyed about a thousand men there.”

target_context_verses.text: After withdrawing seven hundred fifty stadia from there, they reached Charax, among the Jews called Toubiani.
They did not find Timothy in those regions, for he had then left without accomplishing his purpose, but had left a very strong garrison in one place.
Dositheus and Sosipater, commanders under Maccabeus, marched out and destroyed those whom Timothy had left in the stronghold, more than ten thousand men.
Maccabeus arranged his army in companies, placed those men over the companies, and rushed against Timothy, who had with him one hundred twenty thousand infantry and twenty-five hundred horsemen.

When Timothy learned of Judas’s advance, he sent the women, children and remaining baggage ahead to the place called Carnion, for the place was difficult to besiege and difficult to approach because of the narrowness of all the approaches.

When Judas’s first company appeared, dread came upon the enemy. Fear fell upon them through the manifestation of the One who watches all things, and they rushed into flight, scattering in different directions, so that they were often injured by their own men and pierced by the points of their swords.
Judas pursued them with greater vigor, stabbing the accursed men and destroying about thirty thousand.

Timothy himself fell into the hands of Dositheus’s and Sosipater’s men. With much deceitful persuasion he begged them to release him unharmed, because he held the parents of many and the brothers of some, and these would come to be disregarded.
After he had guaranteed in many ways his undertaking to restore them unharmed, they released him for their brothers’ deliverance.

source_context_verses.text: Many of them had been confined in Bosora, Bosor in Alema, Chaspho, Maked, and Carnaim—all these cities were strong and large.
They were also confined in the other cities of Gilead. The enemy had arranged to attack the strongholds the next day, seize them, and destroy all these people in one day.
Judas and his army suddenly turned their route toward Bosora through the wilderness. He seized the city, killed every male with the edge of the sword, took all their spoils, and burned it with fire.
He set out from there by night, and they travelled as far as the stronghold.
In the morning they raised their eyes and saw a great people beyond counting, carrying ladders and siege engines to seize the stronghold and attacking its defenders.
Judas saw that the battle had begun and that the city’s cry rose to heaven with trumpets and a loud shout.
He said to the men of the force, “Fight today for our brothers!”
He came out behind them in three divisions. They sounded the trumpets and cried out in prayer.
Timothy’s army recognized that it was Maccabeus and fled before him. He struck them a great blow, and about eight thousand of their men fell that day.
He turned aside to Alema, attacked it, seized it, killed every male in it, took its spoils, and burned it with fire.
He set out from there and seized Chaspho, Maked, Bosor, and the other cities of Gilead.

A fierce battle took place, and Judas’s men succeeded through God’s help. Defeated, the nomads asked Judas to give them pledges, promising to give livestock and assist them in other matters.
Judas, thinking that they could indeed be useful in many ways, agreed to make peace with them. They received pledges and departed to their tents.
He also attacked a city strong with earthworks and enclosed by walls, inhabited by a mixture of nations, and named Caspin.

target_verses.text: Timothy, who had previously been defeated by the Jews, gathered very numerous foreign forces and assembled not a few horses from Asia. He arrived intending to take Judea by force of arms.
As he approached, Maccabeus and his men sprinkled earth on their heads and girded their waists with sackcloth in supplication to God.
Falling down on the platform opposite the altar, they asked Him to become merciful to them, to be an enemy to their enemies and oppose their opponents, as the law declares.
Rising from their petition, they took up their weapons and advanced some distance from the city. When they had approached the enemy, they remained by themselves.

Just as the sunrise spread, the two sides attacked: the one had, together with courage, their refuge in the Lord as a guarantee of success and victory, while the other appointed anger as the leader of their battles.
As the battle became fierce, five splendid men appeared to the enemy from heaven on horses with golden bridles, leading the Jews.

They took Maccabeus into their midst and sheltered him with their own armour, keeping him unwounded. They hurled arrows and thunderbolts at the enemy, who, confused by blindness and filled with turmoil, were cut down.
Twenty thousand five hundred were slaughtered, and six hundred horsemen.
Timothy himself fled into a stronghold called Gazara, a very strong fortress, where Chaereas was commander.
Maccabeus and his men eagerly besieged the fortress for four days.
Those inside, trusting in the strength of the place, blasphemed excessively and uttered unlawful words.
As the fifth day dawned, twenty young men of Maccabeus’s company, burning with anger because of the blasphemies, attacked the wall courageously and cut down whoever they met with a beast-like fury.

Others likewise climbed up while those inside were distracted, set the towers on fire, and kindled fires that burned the blasphemers alive. Others broke through the gates, admitted the rest of the division, and took possession of the city.
They slaughtered Timothy, who was hiding in a cistern, and his brother Chaereas and Apollophanes.

source_context_verses.text: Timothy’s army recognized that it was Maccabeus and fled before him. He struck them a great blow, and about eight thousand of their men fell that day.
He turned aside to Alema, attacked it, seized it, killed every male in it, took its spoils, and burned it with fire.
He set out from there and seized Chaspho, Maked, Bosor, and the other cities of Gilead.
After these events Timothy gathered another army and encamped opposite Raphon, beyond the stream.
Judas sent men to spy out the camp. They reported to him, saying, “All the nations around us have gathered to him, a very large force.
They have hired Arabs to help them and are encamped beyond the stream, ready to come against you in battle.” Judas went to meet them.
As Judas and his army approached the watercourse, Timothy said to his army commanders, “If he crosses over to us first, we will not be able to stand against him; he will surely prevail against us.
But if he becomes afraid and encamps beyond the river, we will cross over to him and prevail against him.”
When Judas approached the watercourse, he stationed the officers of the people at the stream and commanded them, saying, “Do not allow anyone to encamp; let everyone come into the battle.”
He crossed over against them first, with all the people behind him. All the nations were crushed before them; they threw away their weapons and fled to the sacred precinct of Carnaim.
They seized the city and burned the sacred precinct with everyone inside. Carnaim was overthrown, and they could no longer stand before Judas.

Calling upon the Sovereign who powerfully shatters the strength of enemies, they brought the city under their control and struck down about twenty-five thousand of those inside.
